I read all 261 lines of the target file. I also read the definitions it depends on: maskedPoolCode, maskedPoolCode_decode, rawPoolLeading and stageLeading in ComplexPrefixSeparationPolynomialStage.lean; poolEnumeration in ComplexLabelHierarchySeparation.lean; and conditionalFinset, conditionalPoolEquivFin, appendCode, appendCode_val and decodedFine_eq_geometryDecode in ComplexConditionalPrefixWords.lean. I searched the repository for every downstream use of decodePool, actualPool, actualPool_card, decodedLeading, rawPoolLeading_eq_decodedLeading and nextPrefixDecoder. The main consumers are Completion/GeometricValues.lean and ComplexBounds/CW75ReorderedGeometricValues.lean. nextPrefixDecoder and surviving_nextPrefix have no uses outside this file.

I did not recommend some other changes:
- decodePool_eq_iff should not be a simp lemma. Its right-hand side contains `positive`, which does not occur on the left, so simp could not fill it in.
- decodePool_mem could be tagged @[simp], but nothing downstream needs it, so the evidence is too weak.
- The ExecutionStage and exists_actualPoolStage declarations are existence statements and do not affect the simp interface.

Remaining uncertainty: I could not run Lean. I expect the proposed general bridge lemma to hold by `rfl` for any priorWord, because both downstream files prove the `priorWord = id` case by `rfl` and the unfolding does not depend on priorWord. I have not confirmed that it compiles, and the same applies to the proposed decodedLeading_apply.

findings.problem: The file uses two different forms for the same decoded label. Its own lemmas write it as `decodePool (actualPool counts labels n t priorWord) (stageRefinementCount …) (actualPool_card …) p q`. The imported library's simp lemma `appendCode_val` writes it as `((conditionalPoolEquivFin old).symm code).val`. Since `nextPrefixDecoder` is defined as `appendCode (priorWord p.1) p.2`, both forms describe the same object, but no lemma in the file connects them. As a result, every consumer has to prove the connection itself. Both downstream geometric-value files contain an identical private copy, `actualPool_decode … := rfl`, specialised to `priorWord = id`. Each then needs a second wrapper, `decode_eq_iff_eligible`, to reach the `conditionalPoolEquivFin` statements in HierarchyWords/CW75ReorderedWords.
findings.proposed_change:
Add the general lemma once in this file, right after `actualPool_card`:
```lean
@[simp] theorem decodePool_actualPool
    (priorWord : Prefix → ExactPrefix counts labels n t Position) (p : Prefix)
    (q : Fin (stageRefinementCount counts labels n t)) :
    decodePool (actualPool counts labels n t priorWord)
        (stageRefinementCount counts labels n t)
        (actualPool_card counts labels n t priorWord) p q =
      ((conditionalPoolEquivFin (priorWord p)).symm q).val := rfl
```
This rewrites toward the form used by `appendCode_val`, so it does not compete with existing rules: `conditionalPoolEquivFin` already has its own simp lemmas, and none of them produce `decodePool`. Optionally, restate `nextPrefixDecoder_val` with the `conditionalPoolEquivFin` form, or add `@[simp] nextPrefixDecoder_apply : nextPrefixDecoder … (p, q) = appendCode (priorWord p) q := rfl` so that `appendCode_val` handles it directly. Then delete the two duplicated `actualPool_decode` lemmas downstream.
findings.benefit: The decoded-label expression gets one canonical form that matches the existing `appendCode_val` simp set. This removes duplicated `rfl` bridges in downstream files. It also lets `simp` or `rw` move from `decodedLeading` guards to the `appendCode`/eligibility statements without unfolding definitions by hand.

findings.problem: `decodedLeading` is defined with a tactic block (`by classical; exact fun …`) and has no evaluation lemma. Consumers can only work with it by unfolding the definition. In all six downstream normalisation proofs, the step right after `rw [rawPoolLeading_eq_decodedLeading …]` is `unfold decodedLeading`, followed by `simp only` on the exposed `ite`. Inside this file, `surviving_nextPrefix` also calls `simp [decodedLeading, h]`. Each consumer therefore depends on the internal lambda and on whatever `Decidable` instance the `classical` block happened to choose, rather than on a stated equation.
findings.proposed_change:
Add an evaluation lemma with the guard stated explicitly, for example:
```lean
theorem decodedLeading_apply (pool : Prefix → Finset RawLabel) (k : ℕ)
    (counts : ∀ p, (pool p).card = k) (fine : Prefix → X → Y → Z → RawLabel)
    (p : Prefix) (x : X × InformedOutput k) (y : Y × InformedOutput k)
    (z : Z × MissingOutput k) [Decidable (x.2.1 = y.2.1 ∧ x.2.1 = z.2.1 ∧
      decodePool pool k counts p x.2.1 = fine p x.1 y.1 z.1 ∧ x.2.2 = y.2.2)] :
    decodedLeading pool k counts fine p x y z =
      if x.2.1 = y.2.1 ∧ x.2.1 = z.2.1 ∧
        decodePool pool k counts p x.2.1 = fine p x.1 y.1 z.1 ∧ x.2.2 = y.2.2
      then 1 else 0 := by
  unfold decodedLeading; congr
```
This could also be stated with a classical instance and proved by `rfl`. Downstream proofs would then use `rw [rawPoolLeading_eq_decodedLeading …, decodedLeading_apply]` instead of `unfold`. Because the right-hand side is an `ite` rather than another `decodedLeading`, the rewrite terminates.
findings.benefit: Consumers get a stable rewrite target that does not depend on how the definition body was elaborated. The six downstream proofs and `surviving_nextPrefix` would no longer need to unfold the definition, and changing the definition's internals later would not break them.
